purpose: Meclizine is used to treat and prevent nausea, vomiting, and dizziness caused by motion sickness. It is also commonly used to help relieve the spinning sensation and dizziness that comes with vertigo. Many people find it very helpful when traveling by car, boat, or airplane.
how_it_works: Your brain has a special area called the vestibular system that helps control your sense of balance. When this system gets mixed signals — like when you are on a moving vehicle — it can cause nausea and dizziness. Meclizine works by blocking certain chemical signals in your brain that trigger those uncomfortable feelings, helping you feel more settled and steady.
common_side_effects: The most common side effect is drowsiness or feeling sleepy, which is why some people take it at bedtime. You may also notice a dry mouth, dry eyes, blurred vision, or feeling a little tired or sluggish. Most of these effects are mild and tend to go away as your body adjusts.
warnings: Because meclizine can make you drowsy, avoid driving or operating heavy machinery until you know how it affects you. Alcohol and other sedatives can make the drowsiness much worse, so try to avoid them while taking this medicine. Talk to your doctor before using meclizine if you have glaucoma, an enlarged prostate, liver problems, or if you are pregnant or breastfeeding. Also let your pharmacist know all other medications you take to avoid interactions.
typical_dosing: For motion sickness, adults typically take 25 to 50 mg about one hour before travel, and it can be repeated every 24 hours as needed. For vertigo, the usual dose is 25 to 100 mg per day, divided into smaller doses as directed by your doctor. Always follow the directions on your prescription or package label, and ask your pharmacist if you have any questions.
